5. [USER] Although the three communities we worked with differ in important ways, there were a few things they had in common when it comes to their information needs.
6. [USER] First, all three communities expressed a desire for some form of “service journalism,” whether it was in the form of more information about the location and content of municipal government meetings, how to find service providers, or contact information for local leaders.
7. [USER] Content like this may seem like low-hanging fruit, but publishers who can keep up-to-date and reliable lists like this would provide tangible benefit to their communities.
8. [USER] Second, we learned that people in all three communities rely heavily on Facebook for news and information about their towns and the people in them.
9. [USER] While not everyone enjoys the often partisan or misleading information that circulates so easily on Facebook, it is still one of the first to be updated when news breaks and one of the best places for publishers to be highly visible.
10. [USER] Finally, in two of the three communities – Paterson and Trenton – people want more local news about crime and safety.
11. [USER] In two others – Paterson and Blairstown – the publishers may grow their audience if they offer their content in languages other than English.
12. [USER] In all three, at least some people mentioned wanting more feel-good, solutions-oriented local news.
13. [USER] One lesson learned was that it is difficult to “parachute” in to a community and expect to get a robust response to surveys or focus groups.
14. [USER] Even though our publishers – who themselves are deeply rooted in their communities – assisted in recruiting people, we likely could have benefitted from more face time in the locations and more creative outreach to bring people to the table.
15. [USER] Despite the challenges, all three publishers were deeply appreciative of the opportunity to better understand their audiences at the formative early stage of their development.
16. [USER] Our hope is that the connection they have forged with their audience will continue to become an iterative feedback loop.
